title: Tailoring
coreMove: A team tailors well by reading context, using diagnostics, and revisiting practices so rigor grows or shrinks as evidence changes.

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads choosing where scarce setup attention goes
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may spend its only planning hour copying a plan that does not fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Roman allocates scarce planning time before any execution begins.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders balancing clinical feedback with compliance control
exampleSpecs.stakes: either speed or assurance can fail if the approach treats one pressure as the whole project
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Gage faces two bad options and uses diagnostics to build fit.

exampleSpecs.audience: sponsors and product leads challenging copied plans
exampleSpecs.stakes: a familiar approach may hide the current project's stakeholder needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Eleni and Navid let the tailoring lesson emerge through their exchange.

exampleSpecs.audience: steering teams reading diagnostic signals against expectations
exampleSpecs.stakes: a low headline risk score may hide the need for more feedback
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hassan reveals that diagnostics call for more feedback, not less oversight.

exampleSpecs.audience: project coordinators turning informal complaints into diagnostic evidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may cut a packet without preserving the controls the context still needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sora and Megan use a short message exchange to connect artifact changes to diagnostics.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a familiar checklist may outrun the evidence from a changed release cadence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan interrupts a routine and deliberately restarts from context.
